chapter: Church, Bel Canto and the return to music
title: Father Crowley and friends feeding her
summary: Father Crowley called her a saint; she housed and fed people and Dizzy and Lorraine Gillespie sent food.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Father Crowley, he was concerned about, after he heard I had stopped playing, he was traveling around with the Newport Jazz Festival and Father O'Connor. They both were friends. So he began coming around to try to get me out to play. He came to the house and he told Dizzy and Elaine, "Mary is a saint." They said, "Why would you say this?" He said, "You should go to her house." I had people in here from the Welfare and everywhere and I was sleeping on the floor. I was feeding and clothing them and doing a lot of things with them, you know.
Now you weren't working at this point?
Where did you get the money to feed and clothe them?

I had royalties coming in and friends helped, especially Dizzy Gillespie and Lorraine. I never asked them for anything in my life, but it seems like they were in tune with me. Days I thought I wouldn't have anything to eat - Dizzy's cousin (or a nephew), his name is Boo Frazier - he'd ring the doorbell and he'd have a basket full of food for me - hams, steaks, and a lot of things in there. Lorraine said, "I thought you were hungry so I sent you some food." They were really beautiful; they looked after me and they were so kind to me.
